overview: Two antigen-presentation systems that tell T cells whether a threat is hiding inside a cell or lurking outside it.
genZNote: Everyone's cells report in. Only some cells brief the responders.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Molecules expressed on nearly all nucleated cells, presenting endogenous (intracellular) peptide antigens.
aspects.valueB: Molecules expressed mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells, presenting exogenous (extracellular/phagocytosed) peptide antigens.

aspects.label: Cellular Expression
aspects.valueB: Restricted mainly to dendritic cells, macrophages, and B cells.

aspects.label: Antigen Source
aspects.valueA: Endogenous — proteins synthesized within the cell (e.g. viral proteins during infection).
aspects.valueB: Exogenous — proteins engulfed and processed from outside the cell.

aspects.label: T Cell Interaction
aspects.valueA: Presents to CD8+ cytotoxic T cells.
aspects.valueB: Presents to CD4+ helper T cells.

aspects.label: Processing Pathway
aspects.valueA: Proteasome degrades cytosolic protein; peptides are loaded in the endoplasmic reticulum via TAP transporters.
aspects.valueB: Phagolysosome degrades engulfed protein; peptides are loaded onto MHC II in a specialized vesicular compartment.

aspects.label: Biological Purpose
aspects.valueA: Allows any infected cell to signal 'I'm infected' for direct cytotoxic killing.
aspects.valueB: Allows antigen-presenting cells to activate helper T cells and orchestrate the broader immune response.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: On all nucleated cells, presents intracellular antigen to CD8+ T cells.
aspects.valueB: On antigen-presenting cells only, presents extracellular antigen to CD4+ T cells.
